provenance.scope: 29 complete review records recovered from tool history: 24 article-text reviews and 5 partial interactive reviews. The source thread reports 29 article-text reviews overall; five additional complete records could not be recovered because tool output truncated. No corpus-wide completion or new source review is claimed. Notes are prior analyst assessments, not original article text.

reviews.verdict: retain: practitioner mechanism, version checks required
reviews.claim: Drones have different jobs in preparation, entry, clearing, flank watch, and post-plant; useful information must be converted into action before the defender can reposition.
reviews.specific_evidence: The guide contrasts scouting an entire route alone with a teammate following a drone; it also explains why spotting may warn a defender and when distraction makes that warning useful.
reviews.design_inference: Evaluate information-to-action latency and safe scouting positions. An observation opening is strategically useful only if someone can exploit its information before it becomes stale.
reviews.counter_test: Compare distant pre-scouting, near-term scouting, and paired scout/entry play while varying defender escape routes. Record information age when the mover commits.
reviews.limits: Player advice, not a controlled study; older operator and objective-notification details need current-version checks. Embedded instructional videos were not reviewed.
reviews.prior_card_change: Expand the earlier rotation note to include information age, warning the opponent, and the cost of leaving the scout's body exposed.
reviews.anchors: Preparation phase droning; Scouting for yourself; Scouting in squad; Distraction; Defuser Watch

reviews.verdict: retain: conditional player workflow
reviews.claim: Attacks commonly move through approach, breach-and-clear, and objective push, but rushing is an explicit exception. Breaching and off-site clearing can happen in parallel.
reviews.specific_evidence: The article assigns survival priorities to utility-critical operators, separates breach and map-clear groups, and contrasts completing the objective with seeking eliminations under different late-round states.
reviews.design_inference: Design routes and tools around task dependencies and handoffs. The useful decision is whether the team has created an exploitable opportunity, not whether a universal timer says to advance.
reviews.counter_test: Hold geometry constant and vary breach completion, roamer presence, defuser possession, and remaining time. Check whether players change the order or abandon a preparation task rationally.
reviews.limits: Suggested phase durations and role assignments are coaching heuristics, not measured optimal schedules. Do not encode a single prescribed sequence into every map.
reviews.prior_card_change: Replace generic timing advice with a branching, partly parallel attack workflow and its exceptions.
reviews.anchors: Approach; Breach & Clear; Objective push

reviews.verdict: retain: overview with dependencies and caveats
reviews.claim: Attack preparation combines team roles, useful drone placement, a breach plan, and a deliberate decision to hunt or bypass roamers.
reviews.specific_evidence: The article ties spawn selection to a player's task, orders breach targets by access and utility, and warns that creating an unnecessary angle can hurt attackers later.
reviews.design_inference: Treat access creation as a dependency graph with opportunity costs. Opening a surface should unlock a useful action while potentially changing friendly exposure or drawing defenders.
reviews.counter_test: Remove the expected breaching or support capability and test whether teams can substitute another route, spend more time, or change their objective plan.
reviews.limits: The guide is broad player instruction and overlaps companion articles. Operator counts, gadget availability, and mode timings are version-dependent; claims of universal role necessity are not established.
reviews.prior_card_change: Add substitution, task-specific spawn choice, and the possibility that an attacker-created opening backfires.
reviews.anchors: Operators setup; SPAWN POINTS; Clearing Roamers; Unique Utility

reviews.verdict: retain: highly relevant conditional positioning questions
reviews.claim: Defenders should delay the attack while retaining the ability to change position, cover other entries, and coordinate distinct jobs. Protection can conflict with recovery access.
reviews.specific_evidence: The anchor checklist asks about exposed angles, escape, access to other entries, and teammate coverage; hatch reinforcement has an explicit exception when the plan holds from above.
reviews.design_inference: Evaluate a hold as a bundle of coverage, escape, and response options. Reinforcement is valuable relative to the intended defensive plan, not intrinsically better than an opening.
reviews.counter_test: Compare anchoring below versus holding above, then remove an ally or change the attack direction. Check which wall state preserves a useful response.
reviews.limits: The source includes broad prohibitions and old gadget recommendations; these should not become universal geometry rules. It supplies reasoning, not comparative match data.
reviews.prior_card_change: Upgrade from generic defense coding to the source's explicit four-question positioning test and exceptions.
reviews.anchors: Reinforcements; Anchor's positioning; Carrier denial exception; INTEL GATHERING

reviews.verdict: retain: branching decision with important assumptions
reviews.claim: Whether to hunt roamers or attack the site depends on defender distribution, control of necessary areas, available time, and how easily the flank can be contained.
reviews.specific_evidence: The guide contrasts attacking an under-defended site with clearing a smaller roaming force, then describes locating, containing, and jointly pressuring a roamer through different angles.
reviews.design_inference: A good level supports both bypass-and-contain and search-and-clear plans. Off-site defenders should create a credible choice rather than forcing the same clearing ritual every round.
reviews.counter_test: Vary actual defender distribution and the accuracy of attacker information. Test whether a team can bypass a roamer while covering the relevant return route.
reviews.limits: Inferring role directly from operator choice is unreliable; numerical roamer thresholds are heuristics. Some tool details, including grenade behavior, are historical.
reviews.prior_card_change: Add the bypass branch and information uncertainty instead of presenting containment as the only desirable workflow.
reviews.anchors: When to hunt roamers; Determining the number of roamers; Hunting roamers efficiently; Flank watch scenarios

reviews.verdict: retain: distinguish credible threat from consistent impact
reviews.claim: Roaming aims to consume attacker time and attention; a prepared rotation can matter even when unused, but a hidden defender who returns too late may contribute little.
reviews.specific_evidence: The article contrasts disruptive and stealthy roaming, explains pre-opening routes to avoid later noise, and connects return timing to sound, the kill feed, and pressure on site.
reviews.design_inference: Measure route threat, preparation visibility, and return time as well as traversal frequency. A flank is useful when it can influence the objective within the actual response window.
reviews.counter_test: Provide the same alternate route visibly open, secretly open, and closed. Compare attacker flank-watch costs and whether the defender returns in time to matter.
reviews.limits: The article's percentage estimates, fixed role labels, and gadget rankings are unsupported opinion. Its preference for disruptive roaming should be tested across team skill and communication.
reviews.prior_card_change: Add the source's warning that unused or late mobility can be strategically ineffective, despite creating uncertainty.
reviews.anchors: How to roam; Disruptive roam; Stealthy roam; OBSERVE KILL FEED & LISTEN TO GUNFIGHTS; Movement

reviews.verdict: retain: secondary reporting, not outcome validation
reviews.claim: The Hereford rework sought to reduce restrictive internal movement by expanding space and adding rotation options, including another interior staircase.
reviews.specific_evidence: The article identifies control of the old central stairs as a way attackers could trap defenders and reports added circulation as a response.
reviews.design_inference: Test whether one connector allows a team to cut off too much of the level. A bypass can preserve defensive adaptation without needing to improve every firing position.
reviews.counter_test: Compare defender relocation when attackers control the principal stair, with and without an alternate interior connection.
reviews.limits: This is announcement-era journalism with predictions, not a post-release evaluation. Its favorable expectations do not demonstrate that the reworked map succeeded competitively.
reviews.prior_card_change: Retain the connector mechanism but remove any implication of verified improvement after release.
reviews.anchors: Description of the old central staircase; rework circulation changes; distinction between buffs and reworks

reviews.verdict: retain: developer rationale, mixed historical/live page
reviews.claim: The Hereford rework added floor area, destructible surfaces, stairs, and hatches to improve movement; the Consulate buff changed spawn approaches and added a site.
reviews.specific_evidence: The rework section explicitly links new cross-floor connections to rotations. The Consulate section describes moving a wall to reduce early spawn kills.
reviews.design_inference: Separate transition safety, vertical access, and objective viability as distinct problems. A broader rework and a small targeted correction should be evaluated against different hypotheses.
reviews.counter_test: Test a pressured inter-floor relocation separately from a newly spawned player's safe approach; do not combine them into one aggregate win-rate judgment.
reviews.limits: Developer intent is not measured effect. The season is historical, but some operator panels contain updated abilities and loadouts, so the page is not a clean original-version snapshot.
reviews.prior_card_change: Add Consulate's approach-risk rationale and an explicit warning about mixed-era operator information.
reviews.anchors: MAP REWORK: HEREFORD BASE; CONSULATE MAP BUFF

reviews.verdict: correct reference; retain substantive Para Bellum section
reviews.claim: The body describes Operation Para Bellum and the Clubhouse buff: defenders gained an interior second-floor connector, other circulation changes, and objective adjustments.
reviews.specific_evidence: The page explains that defenders previously had to leave the building to move between two upper areas, producing high-risk, low-reward situations.
reviews.design_inference: Identify routes that impose a cost without a corresponding strategic reward. A protected connector can restore an option while preserving familiar map identity and learned callouts.
reviews.counter_test: Keep the destination task fixed and compare the exposed exterior crossing with the new interior connection, including attacker ability to anticipate and contest arrival.
reviews.limits: The page title incorrectly says High Calibre while the URL and body identify Para Bellum. Live operator panels may have changed since the historical release. No controlled before/after results are supplied.
reviews.prior_card_change: Correct the work identity to Operation Para Bellum; the first-pass title was misleading. Preserve the explicit connector rationale rather than relying on the page title.
reviews.anchors: Introductory Para Bellum text; CLUB HOUSE MAP BUFF

reviews.verdict: retain: primary workflow rationale
reviews.claim: Map buffs are focused gameplay changes intended to improve objective viability while preserving the existing structure and recognizable flow.
reviews.specific_evidence: The developer describes the Clubhouse connector, distinguishes buffs from reworks, and names objective selection in Ranked and Pro League as an input to iteration.
reviews.design_inference: Write an objective-specific failure hypothesis and start with the smallest spatial change that could address it. Use selection patterns to locate problems, then test their causes.
reviews.counter_test: After a targeted edit, measure whether the neglected site becomes usable for identifiable reasons, while checking whether a formerly healthy approach became dominant.
reviews.limits: More even objective selection is the stated goal, not proof of equal strategic quality. The article does not disclose a causal analysis or isolate geometry from roster changes.
reviews.prior_card_change: Add the actual selection-based diagnostic and the constraint to preserve existing player knowledge.
reviews.anchors: Surgical gameplay changes; objective pick rate; preserving structure and flow

reviews.verdict: retain: primary evidence of coupled systems changes
reviews.claim: Shadow Legacy changed information tools, reinforcement allocation, breaching access, temporary gadget disabling, and Chalet navigation together.
reviews.specific_evidence: The article describes a new basement connection, an interior staircase, camera placement across surfaces, and an EMP change that made attack timing depend on a temporary disable window.
reviews.design_inference: Retest geometry after tool and resource changes. The same crossing can gain value through information or timing even without moving a wall.
reviews.counter_test: Use a fixed layout and compare permanent removal with temporary disabling of defensive equipment; measure whether attackers can convert the opening into useful control before recovery.
reviews.limits: The many simultaneous changes prevent attribution of outcomes to the map alone. This is a 2020 announcement, so exact operator and gadget details are historical.
reviews.prior_card_change: Expand beyond Chalet rotation to include temporary opportunity windows and reinforcement-budget changes as confounds.
reviews.anchors: Argus camera description; reinforcement pool; EMP grenade rework; Chalet rework

reviews.verdict: retain: primary map and movement changes, historical
reviews.claim: Void Edge changed Oregon connectivity while introducing new ways to traverse and investigate space through Oryx and Iana.
reviews.specific_evidence: The map section adds the Freezer connection and a route bypassing Meeting, while the operator sections describe hatch climbing, wall-breaking costs, and a scouting body that cannot simultaneously move.
reviews.design_inference: Test connectivity for each actor capability and information method. A route's value depends on who can use it, the preparation cost, and whether scouting exposes the real player.
reviews.counter_test: Compare ordinary movement, hatch-capable movement, and remote scouting under the same enemy setup; record which route benefits disappear when the relevant capability is absent.
reviews.limits: The article introduces changes rather than evaluating long-term results. Historical loadouts and ability details must not be treated as current rules without verification.
reviews.prior_card_change: Connect the Oregon changes to actor-specific movement and scouting constraints rather than counting routes alone.
reviews.anchors: ORYX; IANA; OREGON MAP REWORK

reviews.verdict: retain: strong primary design-process case
reviews.claim: Split evolved around making off-site control relevant to sites; iterations corrected an overpowered tower, excessive mid influence, and poorly connected overwatch positions.
reviews.specific_evidence: The authors trace successive tower and connector revisions and explain why their original strategic focal point drew too much combat away from objectives.
reviews.design_inference: Test where an advantage can be converted into objective progress. Importance alone is insufficient: a control position needs bounded influence and useful connections to the task it supports.
reviews.counter_test: Track where teams spend attention and fight across variants, then test whether holding the focal point changes site outcomes without making other areas irrelevant.
reviews.limits: This is a designer retrospective without raw test data or isolated experiments. It concerns historical Split; diagrams and subsequent live revisions require separate visual/version checks.
reviews.prior_card_change: Preserve the conditional-power insight, but add the explicit distinction between a failed execution and a failed design goal.
reviews.anchors: Design philosophy; THE BUILD; MAKING IT REAL

reviews.verdict: retain: strong primary production workflow
reviews.claim: Ascent moved from a design proposal through prolonged greybox iteration, block-in, and art production; encounter dimensions and navigation were tested before final art.
reviews.specific_evidence: The designers identify sightlines, distance, opening width, doors, architectural hierarchy, and a visually clean combat zone as coordinated parts of the process.
reviews.design_inference: Validate decision geometry with actual combat rules before expensive detailing, then use art to reinforce orientation and readability without changing the tested spatial contract.
reviews.counter_test: Compare navigation and target recognition before and after the art pass while replaying the same crossing and angle-clearing scenarios.
reviews.limits: The timeline is descriptive of this project, not a universal schedule. Combat-zone height guidance is game-specific and should not be copied as a general FPS standard.
reviews.prior_card_change: Add the art handoff and readability audit, and explicitly separate project duration from a recommended workflow duration.
reviews.anchors: Incubation; Greybox; Block-in; Art Production; Clean Zone

reviews.verdict: retain: primary rework objectives
reviews.claim: Reworks aim to make more defender sites practical and improve routes for both sides; some maps require core-layout changes rather than local edits.
reviews.specific_evidence: The developer explicitly identifies single-choke access, difficult rotations, problematic spawns, and uneven site viability as reasons to reconsider a map.
reviews.design_inference: Diagnose whether a failure is local or structural before editing. Improve weak alternatives rather than assuming the strongest existing option must always be removed.
reviews.counter_test: Test neglected sites under several credible defensive setups and attack approaches, then determine whether the same bottleneck defeats them all.
reviews.limits: The article supplies criteria and intent, not demonstrated success of a particular rework. Removal from a competitive pool is not itself evidence that a fix is scheduled or feasible.
reviews.prior_card_change: Add the distinction between improving an alternative and weakening the current favorite, plus the local-edit versus rework decision.
reviews.anchors: Goals of reworks; rotation opportunities; rework/removal criteria

reviews.verdict: retain: primary counterexample to universal route safety
reviews.claim: Kafe explored vertical and close-range play, but a roof spawn was removed because it avoided approach risk and made other spawn choices unattractive.
reviews.specific_evidence: The designer explains both the reduced travel time and absence of approach risk for the roof spawn, alongside lessons about windows, runouts, and relocation.
reviews.design_inference: A route should not be simultaneously safest, quickest, and equally useful without a meaningful cost. Removing such an option can restore decisions elsewhere.
reviews.counter_test: Compare spawn-to-task time, exposure, and attainable position across spawns; check whether any option dominates across plausible defender setups.
reviews.limits: The article reports intent and retrospective judgment, not comparative telemetry. It also notes a removed interior rappel feature without enough detail to reconstruct why it failed.
reviews.prior_card_change: Elevate the removed roof spawn as a concrete dominance test instead of retaining only a generic verticality lesson.
reviews.anchors: Conceptualization; spawn lessons; removed roof spawn and elevator shaft

reviews.verdict: retain: primary iteration case
reviews.claim: Fracture's attacker pinch concept needed protected defender circulation and useful neutral spaces before its unusual topology supported viable setups.
reviews.specific_evidence: The retrospective identifies a single early defender rotation, post-plant trapping by utility, and subsequent creation of safer circulation; neutral areas were then tuned for flank or retake use.
reviews.design_inference: Secure the response network before adding more offensive pressure. The same off-site space can change jobs between early contest, flank, and recovery.
reviews.counter_test: Replay the same pinch with alternative defender links and remaining attacker utility; measure whether defenders can relocate without making the initial attack ineffective.
reviews.limits: Designer intent and recollection, without isolated outcome data. Images and art-process percentages are not validated prescriptions for other projects.
reviews.prior_card_change: Add the order of iteration: establish viable defender circulation, then tune the neutral-space choices.
reviews.anchors: EARLY FISSURES; safer rotation; neutral spaces; VISUAL DEVELOPMENT

reviews.verdict: retain: practitioner theory with mode-specific assumptions
reviews.claim: A strong elevated position becomes a decision when something worthwhile draws its holder away and returning carries a cost; attackers also need credible ways to dislodge it.
reviews.specific_evidence: The author contrasts pickups at the power position with pickups below it and explains why an immediately accessible lift can make leaving almost cost-free.
reviews.design_inference: Tune departure incentive, uncertainty, and reacquisition cost together. A secondary route or pickup matters only if it threatens or exceeds the value of staying.
reviews.counter_test: Move the incentive and return path independently; test whether the holder leaves for intelligible reasons and whether an opponent can exploit the absence.
reviews.limits: Opinion, not controlled measurement. The author distinguishes playlist and arena expectations, so broad claims about how much of the map a power position may control are not universal.
reviews.prior_card_change: Replace generic power-position advice with the explicit leave-versus-stay trade and return-cost mechanism.
reviews.anchors: Pickup incentives; MAINTAIN VALUE; playlist versus tournament discussion

reviews.verdict: retain: important mode-specific counterexample
reviews.claim: In CTF, some long sightlines let a defender contribute offensively without abandoning defense, while distinct base entrances and exposed final delivery create different tactical duties.
reviews.specific_evidence: The author uses Narrows to explain simultaneous flag defense and offensive support, then contrasts differentiated ingress routes with a simple see-through base.
reviews.design_inference: Role overlap can be valuable when it creates participation rather than universal control. Evaluate a position against the intended division of labor and the objective's final interaction.
reviews.counter_test: Compare a protected flag stand with an exposed one and measure offensive support, interception opportunity, and defender willingness to leave the base.
reviews.limits: Examples and preferences are not universal requirements. Long-range support may be oppressive under different weapon lethality or team sizes; diagrams and current map versions were not checked.
reviews.prior_card_change: Add the explicit benefit of shared offensive/defensive influence, which qualifies a blanket recommendation to separate all strong roles.
reviews.anchors: MORE THAN DEFENSE PLAY; CROSSING THE FINISH LINE; FORWARD DEFENSE POSITIONS; BASE COMPLEXITY

reviews.verdict: retain as contested design viewpoint, not a recommendation
reviews.claim: Static and dynamic spawning reward different forms of territorial play; the author argues that carefully executed spawn control can add a skill-dependent metagame.
reviews.specific_evidence: The text contrasts pushing a team into its base with dynamic spawns behind the pushing team, and explicitly acknowledges disagreement about whether the resulting punishment is desirable.
reviews.design_inference: Include the spawn system in the spatial model. A forward push can alter future enemy arrival directions, so route value cannot be inferred from current positions alone.
reviews.counter_test: Compare spawn policies with matched teams and mismatched teams; measure recovery options, predictability, agency after spawning, and sustained trapping.
reviews.limits: Normative and speculative argument with no disclosed test data. Claims that spawn trapping is fun or rewards the right skill must be evaluated with the intended audience rather than adopted as a general rule.
reviews.prior_card_change: Downgrade from generic spawning guidance to an explicit tradeoff and counter-hypothesis about fairness and skill expression.
reviews.anchors: REWARDING SKILLED PUSHES; DYNAMIC SPAWNING; SUMMARY

reviews.verdict: retain as a setup checklist; low explanatory depth
reviews.claim: A site setup includes reinforcement order, movement openings, firing apertures, hatch states, tool placement, player assignments, and crossfires.
reviews.specific_evidence: The author explicitly says the chapter is intentionally thin and points readers to other creators for site-specific explanations.
reviews.design_inference: Document the setup as a system of jobs, not a wall diagram alone. Every opening should have a named crossing or firing function and an assigned user.
reviews.counter_test: Remove one player assignment or change a hatch state and check whether the remaining plan still has a coherent response.
reviews.limits: This is a concise learning framework, not independent evidence that a particular setup works. Its Oregon site list does not establish which rotation side is optimal.
reviews.prior_card_change: Reduce evidentiary weight: keep the checklist but do not count it as a detailed spatial analysis or validation of the linked creators.
reviews.anchors: What a Setup Actually Consists Of; Where to Learn the Rest

reviews.verdict: retain: beginner advice with explicit exceptions
reviews.claim: Beginners should preserve inter-site movement and visibility, use the clock, avoid redundant coverage, and make their positions harder to locate.
reviews.specific_evidence: The guide qualifies its warning against inter-site reinforcement by allowing a panel for needed cover or Mira; it also describes changing position after detection and getting information from a destroyed camera.
reviews.design_inference: Protection and mobility should be evaluated together. An apparent rule violation may serve a different job, so record the reason for an opening or reinforcement before judging it.
reviews.counter_test: Compare a fully sealed divider, an open divider, and a mixed protected crossing; vary enemy information and the teammate's task.
reviews.limits: Broad beginner prescriptions and historical equipment advice are not optimal policies for every site. Audio and gadget details require current-build checks.
reviews.prior_card_change: Add the stated mixed-wall exception and the value of changing position after an information event.
reviews.anchors: DON'T REINFORCE BETWEEN BOMBS; MAKE YOURSELF HARD TO LOCATE; CHECK OUTSIDE DEFAULT CAMS

reviews.verdict: text reviewed; visual setup validation pending
reviews.claim: The Kafe setup descriptions use different defensive structures for each site: upper-floor delay and fallback for one, but horizontal extension for another.
reviews.specific_evidence: Reading uses high holes rather than a traversable Laundry opening; Kitchen is described with a Bakery rotate, protected support, and a separate plant-denial connection.
reviews.design_inference: Do not impose one layering recipe on every objective in the same building. Select movement-only, sight-only, and protected connections according to the local attack and recovery jobs.
reviews.counter_test: For the Laundry connection, compare a firing aperture and a traversable hole while testing an attacker hatch drop and a defender retake.
reviews.limits: The exact placements depend on floor plans, screenshots, current operators, and a team's execution. Those visuals have not been checked, and the overview's broad layering slogan is qualified by its own site descriptions.
reviews.prior_card_change: Add the contrast between sites and reject an unconditional rule that every defense should stack above.
reviews.anchors: BOMBSITES: Reading/Fireplace; Kitchen Service/Kitchen Cooking; HOLDING THE SITE

reviews.verdict: text reviewed; visual setup validation pending
reviews.claim: Border's setup descriptions link off-site control, crossfires, fallback, and vertical influence to different objective locations.
reviews.specific_evidence: The Ventilation/Workshop discussion recommends holding upstairs but leaving an exit and conceding that area after a condition changes; other sites use different support positions.
reviews.design_inference: A layered defense needs an exit trigger as well as an initial position. The value of a hold can change when a hatch or another supporting position is lost.
reviews.counter_test: Replay the same hold with the upper-floor exit available and cut off, and with different hatch states; record whether defenders can actually execute the proposed fallback.
reviews.limits: The prose includes sweeping claims about control positions and communication without comparative evidence. Floor-plan images and role-specific details are required before endorsing exact placements.
reviews.prior_card_change: Add the condition for abandoning space and mark the plan as an unvalidated setup example rather than an optimal policy.
reviews.anchors: BOMBSITES; Ventilation/Workshop; HOLDING THE SITE

reviews.verdict: retain as a coordinated setup lead; execution details pending
reviews.claim: The visible plan assigns a shield player outside Garage and complementary defensive jobs behind the wall, with a protected panel and an adjacent opening.
reviews.specific_evidence: The rendered page names operator roles and two wall tasks, but the individual round steps remain behind an interactive selection.
reviews.design_inference: Test external pressure as a team-supported hold, including how an adjacent opening can preserve support while another panel protects it.
reviews.counter_test: Compare the same outside hold with support intact, suppressed, and absent; inspect both attacker and defender sightlines before accepting the wall arrangement.
reviews.limits: Only visible overview, roles, and wall tasks were reviewed. Individual operator sequences, floor-plan overlay, and original creator footage are pending; no outcome claims are accepted.
reviews.prior_card_change: Narrow the earlier broad inference to the visible coordination structure and mark the source incomplete.
reviews.anchors: Visible operator cards; TEAM WALLS; YOUR ROUND placeholder

reviews.verdict: retain as an attributed plan lead; reported success unsupported
reviews.claim: The visible Church plan combines hatch denial, anchor support, and an off-site defender who can return later.
reviews.specific_evidence: The page lists player jobs and reinforcement tasks but shows a success percentage without visible sample size or opponent information; individual round steps are not exposed in the text.
reviews.design_inference: Use the setup to test dependencies between hatch control and defensive return timing, not as proof that the proposed configuration wins.
reviews.counter_test: Remove the roaming player or open one named hatch and compare which anchor jobs become untenable.
reviews.limits: Interactive instructions and diagrams remain unreviewed. A displayed success percentage is not meaningful performance evidence without denominator, selection method, and match context.
reviews.prior_card_change: Explicitly reject treating the displayed win percentage as support for the strategy.
reviews.anchors: Visible operator cards; TEAM WALLS; reported success badge

reviews.verdict: retain as an attack-dependency example; detailed sequence pending
reviews.claim: The visible Clubhouse Bar plan combines upper-floor clearance, vertical pressure, a horizontal breach, flank coverage, and a designated planting task.
reviews.specific_evidence: Different operator cards receive these jobs; the page also names a primary and backup defuser carrier.
reviews.design_inference: Represent attacks as parallel tasks that converge on an objective interaction. Test whether losing one role creates a recoverable adaptation rather than silently invalidating the whole plan.
reviews.counter_test: Delay upper-floor clearance or remove the first defuser carrier, then observe whether the team can change the order, route, or carrier coherently.
reviews.limits: This is an attributed recipe with interactive round instructions and an overlay still pending. It is not measured evidence of superior map design.
reviews.prior_card_change: Retain the dependency structure while withholding endorsement of the exact timing and tool sequence.
reviews.anchors: Visible operator assignments; DEFUSER; PLANT; YOUR ROUND placeholder

reviews.verdict: retain as a conditional wall-and-role example
reviews.claim: The visible Chalet plan preserves selected firing openings and a protected rotation while assigning forward contest and fallback jobs to different players.
reviews.specific_evidence: Wall tasks explicitly distinguish reinforcement from openings; player cards include a forward contest and a later return, but the detailed round sequence is hidden.
reviews.design_inference: A rotation's protection should be judged relative to the teammate positions and the phase in which it must be used.
reviews.counter_test: Vary which forward room is controlled, then test the rotation with the supporting player alive, absent, and forced off the angle.
reviews.limits: The success badge has no visible evidentiary context. Overlay, source footage, and interactive instructions remain pending, so exact left/right placement is not validated.
reviews.prior_card_change: Preserve this as a testable setup example while separating the author's prescription from demonstrated results.
reviews.anchors: Visible roles; TEAM WALLS: KEEP OPEN; fallback label

reviews.verdict: retain as a multi-floor attack lead
reviews.claim: The visible Bank plan combines upper-floor ownership, vertical destruction, a wall breach, flank protection, and a planting position.
reviews.specific_evidence: The plan separates entry, vertical, support, breach, and flank-watch tasks and identifies an alternate defuser carrier.
reviews.design_inference: Multi-floor control becomes interesting when one team's task enables another task, while exposing a cost or delay that opponents can contest.
reviews.counter_test: Hold the wall breach constant and vary upper-floor control; check whether the same plant remains feasible and whether a different route becomes preferable.
reviews.limits: Only the overview and visible assignments were reviewed. Detailed interactions, floor-plan geometry, and the original creator's reasoning remain pending.
reviews.prior_card_change: Keep the dependency hypothesis but do not describe the plan as a fully evaluated execute.
reviews.anchors: Visible operator cards; DEFUSER; PLANT; SPAWN
